messages:
ashley: quick follow-up on the fallback orchestration RFC I posted earlier today. wanted to capture a few tradeoffs we didn't finalize and get a quick alignment.

ashley: TL;DR: propose a tiny probe sync service that coordinates cross-region canary probes and exposes a per-route health scoreboard for the switcher. not a full state machine — think lightweight coordinator + local agent.

sanjay: curious — why not just extend the existing switcher in runtime? more moving pieces means more ops.

ashley: good callout. two reasons: 1) we want rollout decisions to be deterministic across Hosted/Dedicated/Private without pulling heavy control-plane RPCs into the runtime path, 2) probe cadence/aggregation logic will evolve quickly (ML metrics, diff thresholds) and we want to iterate without touching runtime.

elaine: can you give an example of what the probe payload looks like and what the scoreboard contains?

ashley: sure. minimal example:
```
probe: {
  route: "/generate",
  model_variant: "open-ggml:v1-q8",
  latency_ms: 87,
  success: true,
  quality_score: 0.93, // measured against canary prompt set
  ts: 1680000000
}
```
scoreboard exposes rolling aggregates: p50/p95 latency, error-rate, quality-delta vs baseline, probe-count, last-probe-ts.

elaine: ok. how does the local switcher use that? polling? push?

ashley: two modes: push for hosted (central probe sync service posts per-route verdicts), and pull for private (local agent fetches scoreboard snapshot on interval). both modes fall back to local conservative heuristics if sync fails.

ashley: example policy snippet:
```yaml
fallback_policy:
  route: "/generate"
  canary_window: 5m
  min_probes: 30
  latency_threshold_ms: 200
  quality_delta_threshold: -0.05
  decision_rule: "majority_of_metrics_pass"
```

sanjay: sounds reasonable. what about split traffic durability? if we flip routes quickly we could create cache/KV disruptions.

ashley: yep flagged that — plan is to stage canary by header routing first (sticky header for probe sessions) and only do a full route weight change after a cooldown that allows KV priming. we should also include an explicit cache-warm flag in the scoreboard to delay full switch.

elaine: how do we avoid noisy metrics from small sample sizes (cold starts, transient infra blips)?

ashley: the scoreboard keeps sample counts per bucket and requires min_probes. also we'll use EWMA with exponential decay and outlier trimming. the decision rule can require both latency and quality to pass.

elaine: good. ops question — do we expose these rollouts as first-class objects in the console?

ashley: yes — UX will show a per-route rollout view, probe histograms, and a single button to abort/force-fallback. for Dedicated/Private the console will show the last-known scoreboard from the sync agent.

elaine: what about security & telemetry leakage? probes contain prompt/quality info.

ashley: probes should never carry raw prompts — only hashed prompt IDs and metric deltas. for private installs we keep everything in-region; Hosted can opt-in to sending anonymized eval stats.

taylor: question on ordering — if we get conflicting scoreboards (region A says pass, region B says fail), who wins?

ashley: two-tier decision: route-level policy sets locality preference. default: prefer local region, then prefer fallback if majority of regions fail. we also include a conflict-resolution TTL: if conflicting for > 3m escalate to manual review / automatic conservative fallback depending on severity.

sanjay: failure modes: what happens on split-brain between probe-sync leader and local agents?

ashley: design: probe-sync is optional — local agent has health cache and a conservative local policy if it can’t reach coordinator. for Hosted, we run the sync service with leader replica + etcd for metadata so we can detect split-brain quickly. for Private, agent runs in single-node mode and admin controls policy.

elaine: rollout choreography — do we allow incremental percentages (A/B) or only canary routing with probe headers?

ashley: both. probes use dedicated headers to tag canary sessions. percentage rollouts are done by the runtime switcher once scoreboard criteria met. we also propose a ramp plan: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with guards at each step.

ashley: ops hooks: ability to pin a model_variant per-customer, manual override API, and metrics-backed auto-rollback when quality drops > 3% relative to baseline in a sliding 10m window.

elaine: deployment plan? we need a migration path for existing routes and a kill switch.

ashley: phased: (1) deploy agent + scoreboard storage in staging; (2) enable passive probes (no routing changes) for 2 weeks; (3) enable header-based canaries; (4) safe automated ramping with 1st rollout on non-critical routes; (5) enable full auto-fallback. kill switch: enterprise-wide "fallback-disable" toggle in console + API.

ashley: open questions for this thread:
- do we standardize scoreboard schema now or iterate?
- should probe-sync be a library inside control-plane or separate service?
- what sampling strategy for canaries (random vs user-affinity)?

sanjay: my vote: separate service with thin lib for agent is safer. keeps runtime small.

elaine: standardize schema now but keep it extensible (versioned fields).

ashley: noted. tldr: small coordinator + local agent, push/pull modes, conservative local heuristics, explicit cache-warm phase, and console/ops hooks. I'll capture decisions in the RFC follow-up doc and open a prototype PR for the agent.

deploy-bot: deploy "probe-sync-coordinator" v0.1 to staging succeeded :rocket:

ashley: thanks — I'll drop the follow-up doc link in a bit and schedule a sync with eng-runtime and eng-sre to align on leader election and failover SLAs. :calendar:
